commit.message:
fix(browser): reserve text inputs in semantic cap and add send-click submit fallback

Two live-proven P0 defects blocked the supervisor wake engine after the
35304401576.1 update chain healed:

D-P1: a sidebar-heavy ChatGPT surface (pinned chats, projects, scheduled
entries) saturates the 120-target semantic bound with link/button rows alone,
truncating the composer textbox out of the projection. Every wake send then
fails with supervisor_composer_not_unique and the engine silently re-queues
forever (observed live: 33 links + 87 buttons = exactly 120, zero textboxes).
Fix: unique text-input rows are reserved ahead of the bound; the projection
stays capped at 120 rows.

D-P2: the current ChatGPT composer ignores the synthetic Enter keypress used
by submit_after_type (observed live: the typed prompt stayed in the composer
and only a physical SEND-control click submitted it). Fix: Enter stays the
first submit boundary (preserving the zero-geometry background-submit
contract for hidden fleet tabs); when the event-driven outcome latch misses
it, the single SEND control is re-resolved from a fresh tree and clicked
through the same bounded backend-node path as STOP_GENERATION. If Enter did
submit and the latch missed it, the control is already gone and the
re-resolution fails closed, so no second physical effect is possible.

Tests: 4 new contract tests (bounded input reservation incl. sidebar
saturation fixture, ordering, source contracts for the fallback order and
fences). Full suite 2348 / 2346 pass / 0 fail / 2 Windows-only skips.
npm run check clean.
